name: Dependency Scanning Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday dependency scanning work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical dependency scanning tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday dependency scanning work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical dependency scanning tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When dependency scanning guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Prefer the simplest dependency scanning approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Surface known limitations of a chosen dependency scanning approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
4. Prefer explicit, readable dependency scanning solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. When multiple dependency scanning strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Measure before optimizing any dependency scanning bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to dependency scanning (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Keep dependency scanning changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic dependency scanning advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of dependency scanning correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated dependency scanning concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about dependency scanning over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
